verifications.claim: Artemis III is currently targeted for launch in mid-2027, according to NASA.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis III When 2027'; R2: 'slated to launch sometime in 2027'; R3: 'launched by mid-2027'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources, including NASA (R1), directly state or closely match the 2027 target, with R3 specifying mid-2027.

verifications.claim: Artemis III will be a crewed mission aimed at testing rendezvous and docking capabilities with commercial landers in low-Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's Artemis III demonstration mission in low Earth orbit will test... rendezvous and docking capabilities between Orion and private commercial spacecraft'; R5: identical description; R3: 'low-Earth orbit designed to test essential technologies'
verifications.reasoning: NASA sources directly describe the crewed LEO mission for rendezvous/docking with commercial landers.

verifications.claim: As of April 2026, Artemis III launch date is scheduled for 2027.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Updated April 10, 2026... Artemis III... slated to launch sometime in 2027'
verifications.reasoning: Article dated April 2026 explicitly states the 2027 schedule.

verifications.claim: Artemis III crew will launch on the SLS rocket in the Orion spacecraft, as reported by Space.com.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'launch crew in the Orion spacecraft on top of the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket'; R5: 'The Artemis III crew will launch in Orion on the SLS rocket'
verifications.reasoning: NASA sources directly confirm SLS/Orion crew launch for Artemis III; attribution to Space.com not in cited sources but fact faithfully represented.

verifications.claim: Artemis III crew will dock with a commercial lander such as SpaceX’s Starship in low-Earth orbit, as reported by Space.com.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R5: 'test one or both commercial landers from SpaceX and Blue Origin... rendezvous and docking capabilities between Orion and the private commercial spacecraft'; R4: 'SpaceX Starship... lunar lander version that will be used on Artemis 3'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm LEO docking test with SpaceX lander (Starship); attribution not in cited sources but fact supported.

verifications.claim: SpaceNews and The Guardian note that the Artemis III revision follows concerns over technological readiness.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3 (Guardian): 'radical changes... grapples with technical glitches... too risky'; R4 (SpaceNews): 'changing the scope of Artemis 3... if key elements suffer major delays... problems SpaceX has had on Starship'
verifications.reasoning: Both named sources discuss revisions due to technical delays and risks.

verifications.claim: The Artemis III revision focuses on addressing delays in the human landing system (HLS).
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R4: 'concern about the progress SpaceX was making on its Starship vehicle, including the lunar lander version [HLS]'; R3: 'test essential technologies... space vehicles'
verifications.reasoning: Sources link changes to HLS (Starship) delays but in broader terms of technical issues.

verifications.claim: The actual human lunar landing has been shifted to the Artemis IV mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'The Artemis III mission will no longer aim to land on the moon. Instead... a new Artemis IV mission would set out in 2028 to land on the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Directly states shift of landing from III to IV.

verifications.claim: Artemis IV mission is now targeted for 2028.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'a new Artemis IV mission would set out in 2028 to land on the moon'
